summary.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% to INR2,995 crores, but EBITDA was flat at INR222 crores (7.4% margin) on El Niño and input-cost inflation.
summary.overview: Q2 revenue grew 17% YoY to INR2,995 crores, led by animal nutrition, oil palm and B2C food, while EBITDA held at INR222 crores with margin at 7.4%. PBT rose 5% to INR131 crores and PAT rose 22% to INR103 crores. H1 revenue grew 13% to INR5,847 crores, with H1 EBITDA and PBT declining modestly and H1 PAT at INR231 crores. Management said crop care and Astec were hit hard by El Niño and weak demand, and that the FY27 double-digit PBT growth target is now harder to hit.

financial_highlights.value: 21 days (management also cited 22 days in Q&A)
Revenue growth 28%, segment profit growth 4%; FFB volume growth 14%

segments.name: Animal nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue up 14% and segment profit up 32% on realisations and volume gains; margin improved on mix and efficiencies. Volume grew only 3% as broiler feed was deliberately de-prioritised, while cattle feed grew ~8% and layer feed grew double digits. Shrimp feed business exited.

segments.name: Oil palm
segments.commentary: Revenue up 28% and segment profit up 4%; FFB volumes up 14%. Added 13,000 hectares in H1 and commissioned a mill, CPKO refinery and biogas plant at the Khammam integrated complex. Heat stress cut OER to ~18.9% in Q2.

segments.name: Crop care
segments.commentary: Revenue grew on a lower base but profitability fell on El Niño-led demand weakness and adverse product mix. Ashitaka maize herbicide expected to cross INR100 crores revenue in its first year.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: Weak enterprise demand, especially in global markets such as the US and Brazil, offset CDMO growth. EBITDA hit by lower realisations and higher input costs; CDMO share of business targeted at 50-55% over the midterm.

segments.name: Dairy
segments.commentary: Revenue up 6% on calibrated pricing and value-added mix; profitability hit by elevated milk procurement, packaging and logistics costs. No pricing respite expected for the next two quarters.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: B2C revenue up 50% with salience at 38%. EBITDA plus working media margin 5.8% vs 5.6% last year. Around 25% of current business comes from products launched in the last year.

segments.name: ACI Godrej (Bangladesh JV)
segments.commentary: Strong quarter with robust volume, revenue and profit growth; INR50 crores dividend received from the JV in Q2. Management reports double-digit volume growth across aqua, poultry and dairy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit PBT growth is now tougher; management says it will still chase it, with more clarity each month.
Oil palm FFB volume growth guided at double digits for FY27 and FY28, with H1 close to double digit.
Oil palm OER aimed to recover to ~19.7% or more by year-end, which would bring the full-year OER back to last year's level.
PKO derivatives plant gives roughly 2% extra EBITDA margin to oil palm over 2-4 years; meaningful contribution from Q4 and scale-up in FY28.
Oil palm EBITDA targeted at healthy double-digit CAGR in the year and midterm.
Debt-to-equity expected at around 0.8 through H2, with inventory build expected to unwind.
Extra manpower cost for sales transformation to flow into FY27 and annualise in FY28; dairy GTM revamp expected to take about 18 months.
Crop care and Astec expected to take a couple of years to structurally correct.
capex_capacity: Khammam integrated oil palm complex inaugurated: seed/genetics, nursery, R&D, mill, CPKO refinery and biogas plant; full hydrogenation and fractionation due in December.
PKO derivatives plant commissioned on 1 September; second scale-up stage due December; meaningful impact from Q4.
Three new crop care products launching this year; target of seven crop segments by FY29-30.
Dairy GTM pilot (AM/PM distributor model) started in Chennai one month before the call; to be reviewed over the next six months before wider rollout to Andhra and Telangana.
demand_pricing: Monsoon ended about 13% below normal; June rainfall about 40% deficit; reservoirs at a 10-year low, which management says will weigh on the Rabi season and agchem demand.
Palm oil prices expected to stay around INR4,250-4,400 over the next couple of months, then possibly rise from February-March depending on El Niño in Indonesia and Malaysia.
Andhra Pradesh fruit price order for the new year not yet issued; last year's order assumed 20.01% OER, and management hopes the new order sets a lower rate.
Dairy milk prices: management expects no respite for two quarters due to El Niño-led cattle productivity loss, with a structural reset from value-added products.
Frozen chicken, momos (veg momo launched this month) and nuggets are the main B2C growth categories; quick commerce is a tailwind.
Astec CDMO: about 90% of inquiries converted into R&D stage in Q2 and around 15 products in R&D pipeline; 70-80% of R&D products expected to reach commercialisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FFB volume growth target (double digit for FY27 and FY28) still achievable given the heat and cyclones in Andhra Pradesh?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FFB grew double digits in Q2 despite three months of extreme heat, and Q2 collections were a record. Cyclones brought rain and caused no widespread tree damage, so double-digit FFB guidance stands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin contribution from the PKO derivatives plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guides roughly 2% extra EBITDA margin for the oil palm business in the midterm (2-4 years), with the plant starting in September and meaningful impact from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any update on FY27 PBT guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says a double-digit PBT target is harder given El Niño's bigger impact on agchem, but it has not given up. Oil palm EBITDA is targeted at a healthy double-digit CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise by INR200-300 crores vs March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says inventory was built deliberately to capture higher prices amid inflation; this should unwind in H2. Debt-to-equity is about 0.8 and expected to stay around that level.

qa_highlights.question: Why is animal feed volume growth only 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Broiler feed was deliberately de-prioritised, while cattle feed grew ~8% and layer feed grew double digits. Management says the focus should be on those two segments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pricing outlook for dairy?
qa_highlights.answer: No respite expected for the next two quarters; El Niño is cutting cattle productivity and value-added mix shift should cause a structural reset in milk pricing.

risks_watch: Oil palm OER recovery to ~19.7%+ by year-end; the three-month heat impact still shows in Q3 margins.
Andhra Pradesh FRP (fruit price order) for the new year: a rate below 20.01% would help oil palm.
Crop care and Astec demand weakness from El Niño and a tough Rabi season; no clear timeline for turnaround.
Dairy milk procurement inflation for at least two more quarters, and dairy GTM revamp execution over about 18 months.
Rising debt and inventory build in H1; watch whether H2 working capital releases cash.
Rising extra manpower costs for the sales transformation team in FY27 and FY28.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the near term: management openly says agchem, dairy margins and the FY27 PBT target are under pressure. It is more confident on structural levers (oil palm FFB growth, PKO derivatives, B2C foods, CDMO pipeline) and on ACI Godrej's volume growth.
